title: Amendment A1 to B24-CONFIRM-FWD: the confirming close must be $15 to $20 beyond the trigger price
status: REGISTERED 2026-11-10, before B24 started (its recorder is not deployed: nothing has been recorded) and before any code implementing it was written. The original registration is kept byte-identical; this file states the only rule that changes.
approval: Operator, 2026-11-10 (chat): "Confirmation movement must be capped between $15 and $20. The original trigger price must remain fixed from the trigger candle close. BUY confirmation: First qualifying 15-minute candle must close at least $15 above the original trigger price. It must close no more than $20 above the original trigger price. SELL confirmation: [mirrored]. If price moves beyond $20 without a qualifying confirmation, classify the setup as EXPIRED / NO TRADE. Do not accept a $21-$48 movement as confirmation. The -$13 adverse-touch invalidation rule remains unchanged. No trigger-price resetting, retrospective entries or look-ahead." and "Before B24 starts: Amend the registered confirmation rule. Record the amendment in the research log. Preserve the original registration and historical results."
reason: The PR #90 verification round (2026-11-10) recomputed 200 live setups from the raw bars: under the original rule 23 of 72 confirmations closed more than $20 beyond the trigger price (largest $48.05, mean $19.66). The operator does not accept chasing a move that has already gone that far.

replaces.rule.confirmation: On the site's 15m bars that open after the trigger close, bar by bar: (1) price trading $13 against the trigger price (the bar's high / low) or a 15m BOS / MSS / CHoCH printing the other way INVALIDATES the setup; this is checked first on every bar, so a bar that does that and also closes beyond $15 is INVALIDATED. (2) Otherwise the first completed 15m CLOSE at least $15.00 beyond the trigger price in the signal's direction decides: if that close is no more than $20.00 beyond the trigger price the setup is CONFIRMED at that close; if it is more than $20.00 beyond, the setup is EXPIRED (overshoot) and can never be confirmed later. (3) No such close within 96 bars: EXPIRED. Distances are measured from the trigger price, which stays the trigger bar's close and is never reset. Bounds are inclusive and exact to the cent ($15.00 and $20.00 qualify; $14.99 and $20.01 do not); a floating-point tolerance of 1e-9 is the only slack. A touch never confirms, and an intrabar move beyond $20 on its own neither confirms nor expires a setup: only closes confirm or overshoot (stated before any capped result was computed; the operator's 'price moves beyond $20 without a qualifying confirmation' is read on 15m closes, like every other confirmation condition; a wick-based reading would need a further amendment before B24 starts). Each 15m bar is examined once, by the first run that has it (quantum/confirm_panel.py's state machine): a decision, once recorded, is never changed; a later revision of a bar by the data feed is flagged and not applied.

unchanged: Everything else in B24-CONFIRM-FWD.json: the stream (engine signals 15m / 30m / 1h / 4h, one per idea), the trigger price and time, entries A (the confirming close) and B (the first executable price), the costs recorded, the exits (+$15 / +$20; S13 primary, S10, SATR, SSTR; 5m bars; 48 hours), the excursions, the records, the primary test (B executable, +$15 before -$13 net of $0.26, break-even 47.4%), the hypotheses H-ALL / H-BUY / H-SELL, the looks at 30 / 50 / 75 / 100 decided results with their thresholds (21 / 32 / 46 / 59 wins, Wilson z = 2.24), the deadline 2029-12-31, the weekly report and the decisions. The simulated error rates are a property of the looks and thresholds and are unchanged.
expected_pace: Fewer confirmations than the original rule: the cap removes every confirmation whose close was beyond $20. The deadline is not extended; the pace is reported in the weekly report.
scope: The same capped rule is used by the website's confirmation panel (quantum/confirm_panel.py) for every trigger type, so the panel and B24 never disagree on what was confirmed. The panel stays display only and every trigger type stays NOT VALIDATED.
historical_results: Kept as published and labelled as measured under the original rule: B19, B21, research/CF_VALIDATION.md, the panel's EVIDENCE figures. The capped rule's historical figures are reported beside them, never instead, and no rule is chosen by comparing them: the cap is the operator's decision, made before those figures existed.
no_look_ahead: The cap is decided on the same close that would confirm, at that bar's close; no later bar is read. An overshoot is final: a later pullback into the $15-$20 band does not revive the setup (no retrospective entries).
